newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi Kurdish faction captures key northern dam.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurdish faction captures key northern dam.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish faction backed by Baghdad on Monday captured the key Dukan Dam from a rival group in northern Iraq after nearly four hours of fighting, witnesses said.

They said Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) peshmerga guerrillas took the dam in fighting along a 70-km stretch of road, meeting sporadic resistance along the way from the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
Control of the dam is important because of its hydroelectric plant.
About 600 to 700 KDP peshmerga took part in the fighting, using small arms, mortar fire, rocket propelled grenades and truck-mounted anti-aircraft machineguns.
There were very few fixed PUK positions along the highway to the dam, Reuters reporter Kurt Schork said from above the dam. The fighting took the form mainly of hit-and-run skirmishes.

KDP engineers were poised to check the dam for damage. The only sign of damage along the route of the fighting was a number of downed high-tension power lines. Witnesses saw around five KDP fighters injured. A peshmerga from each group was killed in earlier fighting.
